First listed: 2025-11-03 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

- [YouTube: Inside the Cannabis Comeback: How One Company is Beating a Broken Market | The Real Eisman Playbook](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IEhfzy112nE) - 2025-11-03
- [Substack: Inside the Cannabis Comeback: How One Company is Beating a Broken Market | The Real Eisman Playbook](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/inside-the-cannabis-comeback-how-8e7) - 2025-11-03

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Eisman discloses a speculative Glass House holding and explores a low-cost greenhouse producer's profitability, raid recovery and federal-reform upside with management. Production recovery and eventual NYSE listing have evidence, but cash generation remained weak and broad interstate/export upside was conditional. The important legal distinction is that Schedule III alone does not open unrestricted trade; Farrar explicitly qualifies Kazan's earlier overstatement.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

## Framework and tools

- Separate a low-cost operating thesis from a policy catalyst.
- Normalize seasonal costs, nonrecurring profits and disputed taxes before calculating ROE.
- Model volume, realized price and margin separately; more production need not mean more cash.
- Distinguish state permission, federal registration, exchange eligibility and export permits.
- Treat management superlatives and illustrative capacity revenue as assumptions rather than verified forecasts.
- Check whether commodity competition erodes the price spread underlying expansion plans.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Cost per pound and seasonal production
- Gross, operating and adjusted EBITDA margins
- Production recovery versus OCF
- 280E and COGS treatment
- Capacity utilization and price sensitivity

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman interviews CEO Kyle Kazan, president Graham Farrar and CFO Mark Vendetti. Management claims are separated from host adoption and questions.
- All 1242 caption lines were read.
- Opening montage repeats interview claims.
- Names and financial abbreviations have ASR errors;18ish% matches operating margin, not adjusted EBITDA margin.
- Management allegations and compliance representations are not adjudicated facts.
